description: MECHANISM: a `define … end` body is a `repcount` boundary EVEN WHEN the `define` is lexically nested inside a `repeat` and called from inside it (issue #1155). This shape is chosen deliberately, because it is the ONLY one that falsifies the boundary. An earlier draft of this fixture used a top-level `define` called from a `repeat`; that reads clean under a purely lexical walk too, so removing the boundary left the whole 1011-fixture corpus green and the fixture proved nothing — caught in review by mutation, not by reading. Here the procedure body sits inside the `repeat`'s brackets, so without the boundary it would be judged enclosed and this fixture goes green in error. Measured against the evaluator: this exact program raises `ol-repcount-outside-repeat` at `runtime` after 5 events, because a callee's repeat-turn stack starts empty. Note what settles that and what does not: `spec/commands.md:783` ties `repcount` to the ENCLOSING `repeat`, and `spec/execution-model.md:340-342` fixes lexical frame scoping for BINDINGS — but neither spells out `repcount` across a call boundary, and `execute-internal.ts` flags its empty-per-callee stack as an assumption. So this characterizes the evaluator rather than deciding the open question; it was reported to `@orchestrator` at implementation time.
